construct_or_mutation: Limulus polyphemus arginine kinase, uniformly 15N-enriched and 80% 2H-enriched, wild type
other_conditions: 1.0 mM protein, 90% H2O/10% D2O; related structures: 1M80 (substrate-free open crystal structure, used for N-H vectors and domain assignments); the substrate-bound closed structure is discussed but its PDB id is not printed in the text; regime (authors): no assumption of fast or slow exchange; individual fits: D88 kex = 3200 ± 240 s-1, H90 1020 ± 480 s-1, G92 1560 ± 760 s-1; hinge about residues 88-94
timescale: kex = 1930 ± 350 s −1; kopen ≈ 1920 s −1; kclose ≈ 10 s −1; |Δω| = 3.2 ± 0.3 ppm (D88), 4.4 ± 0.6 ppm (H90), 3.4 ± 0.4 ppm (G92) (collective two-state fit of D88, H90, G92)
caveat_note: The card temperature (298.5 K) differs from the printed 25 ± 0.5 °C by less than the printed error; field 600 MHz is among the fields used. The closed-state structure is compared by the authors, but the NMR gives no direct evidence that the excited state is the closed form ('the NMR analysis provides no direct evidence'). The authors note small pB makes the exact fitted values uncertain; kopen and kclose are approximations from kex and pB. Assignment of the minor state as the 'open/closed' form assumes two-state exchange between those forms.
experiment: 15N TROSY constant-time CPMG relaxation dispersion at 15N Larmor frequencies 60.78, 72.95 and 81.04 MHz (1H 600, 720, 800 MHz), two-state Bloch-McConnell fit; N-terminal domain hinge residues
author_claim: Hinge residues report a rigid-body motion of the N-terminal domain at ms rates in substrate-free enzyme; the slower rate (kclose ≈ 10 s-1) is the same order as kcat (100-150 s-1 quoted), so the motion is potentially rate-limiting.
anchor: fitting a single collective motion yields k ex = 1930 ± 350 s −1 and p B = 0.4 ± 0.1%
